result:
Round 278 is planned and dispatched as **SYS-5 stage 2**, the last stage of making unavailable Studio buttons reachable by keyboard. Decision is **CONTINUE**: plenty of scoped work remains, and nothing needs outside input.

**What closed:** C passed round 277 with browser verification and no bugs, and gate 277 published commit `42872cf`. That makes SYS-5 stage 1 (the seven transport buttons) done (მზადაა) and closes GATE276-T1, C-R229-01 and GATE229-S1. The 3-day regression isn't due until 2026-11-02. The old task is copied to `tasks/round-277.md`.

**What round 278 asks A to build** (baseline `42872cf`, 20 granted files, 1,122 frozen):
- **Metronome toggle:** when there is no BPM it becomes focusable with its reason in the title, instead of natively disabled. One exception to the shared pattern: if you type a BPM and click Metronome without pressing Enter, one click still commits the tempo and turns it on. I measured that this is exactly what happens today; the shared pattern would have turned that click into a dead one. On an invalid BPM, focus now lands on the toggle instead of the page body.
- **Library Preview and Add:** both get the same treatment. Add now has a title in every state, e.g. "Add — make an audio track active first".
  - Preview was a disagreement: tech-lead wanted to leave it for later, product-designer wanted it included so Tab treats both buttons the same. I went with product-designer.
- **One shared helper** in `studio-soft-disabled.ts`, with a click guard used by all ten buttons. This settles A's architecture note from round 276.
- **Stage-1 leftovers:** unavailable buttons now show a not-allowed cursor instead of a pointer (C-R276-01). The unavailable Delete button is named plainly "Delete" (A-R276-REVIEW-DELETE-NAME).
- **Perf harness:** three perf specs waited for the Add button to be enabled; after this change that check would always pass early, so they now read the new attribute.
- **Docs:** doc 206 is closed and doc 207 is new.

**Why the gate shouldn't fail again like round 276:** I applied the whole change, including the test updates, to a scratch copy and ran it before writing the task.
- The full test suite passed (220 files, 3,294 tests), and typecheck and lint were clean.
- Five deliberately broken versions each made at least one test fail.
- A second dev server let me compare the change with the current build in a real browser. The cursor fix works, the new focus stops appear, and the look is within the accepted ΔE2000 ≤ 3 (worst 2.83).

The scratch copy was deleted after the saved diff checked byte-identical.

**One tooling finding:** Playwright's `click()` waits forever on these buttons. C's instructions now say to use a raw mouse click, and I added a line to lessons L25.

**Root:** SYS-5 is a feature boundary, so I filed one optional, non-blocking architecture checkpoint, ARCH-CHECKPOINT-SYS5-SOFT-DISABLED. It asks whether the helper should later become a prop on the shared Button.

**Next:** if C passes and the gate publishes, SYS-5 is fully done. Round 279 is then the next performance task (PERF b-ii), unless that planning falls on or after 2026-11-02, when the regression round goes first.

**Advisor:** it was available, and I consulted it before choosing the approach and again before finishing.

The backlog and feature-status updates are recorded under decisions D-29z624 to D-29z633, with backups in `b-round-277/`.
